title: China's humanoid robot shipments hit 97% of the world as Tesla stalls
key_facts: Global humanoid robot shipments reached roughly 19,100 units in the first half of 2026, more than triple about 5,100 a year earlier.
Chinese makers account for more than 97% of volume, led by AgiBot, Unitree and UBTech.
Tesla's Optimus aimed to build 5,000 units in 2025 and managed only a few hundred, held up largely by the hand and arm.
A Unitree G1 sells for $13,500 and its R1 model for $4,900.
Robots deployed by BYD and Foxconn reach only 30% to 50% of human productivity, according to the article.
China's National Development and Reform Commission has warned of overheating in the humanoid market.
Morgan Stanley projects a $5 trillion global humanoid market, which the article calls uncertain.
quote_evidence: Global humanoid robot shipments reached roughly 19,100 units in the first half of 2026, more than triple the roughly 5,100 units shipped in the same period a year earlier, with Chinese manufacturers accounting for more than 97% of volume.
Whether the $5 trillion figure holds up over a decade is genuinely uncertain.

China's National Development and Reform Commission has warned of overheating in the humanoid robot market, the kind of language regulators use right before a bubble gets painful for the companies that overbuilt capacity.
why_it_matters_hint: Chinese makers dominate humanoid production volume while US firms lead on AI software, according to the article.
event_date: First half of 2026 data; article 14 Oct 2026
notes: Original data sources are not named; the article itself contains inconsistent Unitree valuation figures ($50 billion and $6.2 billion), so no valuation is used.
